testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should happen before air pressure in an air brake tank drops below 55 psi?

options.text: The warning light should turn on.
The vehicle will not shift out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The warning light should turn on.
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning light must turn on before air pressure drops below 55 psi. If the warning light does not work during an inspection, the vehicle is not safe to drive.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within ____ seconds.
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection with a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in both systems. This takes about 45 seconds.

questions.question: An alcohol evaporator is especially important:
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to prevent ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: Foundation brakes are used:
questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are on every wheel. The most common type is the s-cam drum brake.

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located inside:
questions.explanation: Brake drums are attached to the wheels on the axles. The parts that make the vehicle stop are inside the drum brake.

questions.question: Using an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) helps you control the vehicle during hard braking. It does not make the vehicle stop faster.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Does not work with air brakes.
Does not help in most driving situations.
Helps you stay in control when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps you stay in control when braking.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) work with air brakes and prevent the wheels from locking up. This helps you keep control of the vehicle.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in the air brake system releases air:

options.text: Something is wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air if pressure gets too high. If this happens, the system has a problem that needs to be fixed by a mechanic.

questions.question: If using spring brakes with a heavy load, a complete stop will:
questions.explanation: Spring brakes do not work on all axles. When they activate due to low air pressure, the vehicle needs more distance to stop, especially with a heavy load.

questions.question: In S-cam brakes, rods move the slack adjusters when air pressure is added to the brake chambers. This happens when the driver:
questions.explanation: When the brake pedal is pressed, air enters the brake chambers. The air pressure pushes the rods and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning signal:

options.text: Is not recommended on vehicles with air brakes.
Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
Is optional on vehicles with air brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal.

questions.question: Having ABS on only one axle:

options.text: Still gives you more control when braking.
Slows the vehicle, but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Still gives you more control when braking.
questions.explanation: If only one axle has ABS, you still have better brake control than without it. Brake normally.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, a single vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than ____ in one minute.
questions.explanation: The air brake system should not lose more than 2 psi in one minute. If it does, something needs repair and the vehicle should not be driven.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, the driver should:

options.text: Pull out the air brake knob.

questions.explanation: To stop, simply press the brake pedal down.

questions.question: When parking, do not use the parking brake if:

options.text: There is snow on the ground.

questions.explanation: Hot brakes can be damaged by the parking brake. Let them cool first before parking.

questions.question: Brakes go out of adjustment quickly when:
questions.explanation: Hot brakes lose adjustment quickly. Check your brake adjustment regularly. All brakes must work properly and be adjusted correctly for safe vehicle control.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and oil that can damage the system. Air tank drain valves help remove this water and oil.

questions.question: Alcohol evaporators:

options.text: Add alcohol to air brake systems.
Are only allowed in northern parts of the state.

questions.correctAnswerText: Add alcohol to air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have alcohol evaporators that add alcohol to prevent ice formation.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning signal should activate when tank pressure falls below:
questions.explanation: The warning signal must activate when pressure drops below 55 psi. It may be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: Air tank drains should:

options.text: Only be used when it is wet outside.

questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and oil from the tanks. Drain them completely each time.

questions.question: What prevents wheels from locking up when braking?
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops the wheels from locking up when you brake.

questions.question: While driving, ____ keeps spring brakes in place.
questions.explanation: While driving, air pressure holds spring brakes in place. If air pressure drops low enough, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: A dual air brake system:

options.text: Has two separate air brake systems that use one set of controls.
Is one air brake system with two different sets of controls.
Has one system for the left side of the truck and one for the right side, each with its own controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has two separate air brake systems that use one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. Both systems share one set of brake controls. Each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines. One system usually controls the regular brakes on the rear axle. The other system usually controls the regular brakes on the front axle.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning signal comes on, you should:

options.text: Keep driving and have the brakes fixed within a week.
Stop safely and check the brakes.
Call a mechanic while you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely and check the brakes.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning comes on while driving a vehicle with air brakes, stop safely as soon as you can still control the brakes. Check and repair the brakes right away.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air brakes have three systems: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. Emergency and parking brakes use mechanical force.
